D006-D005_h001.question:
I’ve been like this maybe around a year, but it’s hard to tell where it really started. At work on the night shift, I’ll get these times where I see people in the lot—standing by the pumps, staring at me—but when I look again, nobody’s there. Sometimes it’s shapes, like shadows moving along the shelves. It makes me feel like the security cameras or the radio are talking about me, like the songs or little comments on TV are somehow aimed at me specifically.

My mood is all over the place. Some nights I feel wired and amazing, like I can clean the whole store, rearrange the shelves, plan out my whole life all at once. I’ll start counting stock, then suddenly I’m outside wiping pumps, then I’m halfway through reorganizing the cooler and none of it gets finished. Other times, a customer says one small thing and I snap inside and get really irritated.

Then I’ll crash for days where I don’t enjoy anything—games, hanging out, nothing feels good. I go to work because I have to, but it’s like I’m not really there. I’ve had these strong urges, like when a car speeds by, I picture stepping in front of it, or standing on a high place and thinking about jumping, even if I don’t actually plan it. Sometimes my words start rhyming by accident, like my mouth is chasing the sound instead of what I’m trying to say, and people look at me weird.
